key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within minutes to hours. LOCATION: UNILATERAL weakness, numbness, or paralysis. DURATION: Immediate onset, symptoms persist. CHARACTER: SUDDEN, SEVERE weakness, numbness, or paralysis. AGGRAVATING: MOVEMENT, speaking, swallowing. RELIEVING: IMMEDIATE medical intervention, thrombolytics if within window. TIMING: Sudden onset, symptoms persist. SEVERITY: 8-10/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: FACIAL DROOP, arm weakness, speech difficulty, vision problems, dizziness, confusion, headache. KEY POSITIVES: Positive FAST test (Face, Arm, Speech, Time), unilateral weakness, facial droop, speech difficulty. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no photophobia.

red_flags: Sudden severe headache with neck stiffness - possible hemorrhagic stroke, call 911
Severe neurological deficits with altered mental status - possible large stroke, call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
